request:
Rana asks the following (complete latest transcription):

"And with regards to SQLite selection, including its bundled C implementation, are there any modern alternatives that might be more efficient, effective, functional, or more performant? What is in the Rust ecosystem that might be comparable with a similar footprint or embedding or functionality? You know, what is the feature matrix that we would like to see."

Please independently challenge Continuum's storage choice using the supplied current facts. In about 650 words: identify the decisive feature requirements, strongest case for changing and for retaining SQLite, an overlooked integration/semantic risk, and the smallest informative next comparison. Distinguish a Rust SQL implementation from a Rust KV substrate; do not assign an unsupported speed winner. Address whether removing the bundled C database engine is valuable in itself and how storage ownership affects independent CLI processes. End with a concrete conditional recommendation.
context:
Project/source facts inspected at public rana/continuum commit 3d15a37fa7faeb53dde9f7ad517c72d99b9b771b: MIT Rust native work/evidence engine, current library+JSON CLI. rusqlite0.40.2 bundled libsqlite3-sys0.38.2 cache contains SQLite3.53.2 source. This is source inspection, not a new runtime version query. Immutable exact encoded blobs/snapshots/evidence IDs; objects table, heads keyed(acceptor,target) with root+generation, operations keyed(acceptor,operation_id) retain exact request and receipt. Acceptance runs short BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction: bind request identity, check expected head/generation/candidate, update head and insert receipt atomically. Exact retry must recover historical result after head moves; changed request with same operationID fails. Current CLI processes independently open the same DB; Store::open itself obtains BEGIN IMMEDIATE even for read commands to check/init format. Tables STRICT, compound PKs, CHECK generation>0, FK root->objects, ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, immutable-table BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers RAISE(ABORT). No WITHOUT ROWID. WAL + FULL sync +5sec busy timeout. Current baseline:20scenario tests with two process-crash cases;3processes each100samples×9groups, small single-worker API timings exclude database startup; overlayfs Chat executor, not user workstation or high-load/language comparison. Current selected product milestone is real-use checkpoint/successor handoff, no persistent workstation deployment yet.

Current upstream primary-document summaries (no candidate executed): redb4.4.0 Oct13,2026, pure-Rust embedded copy-on-write B+tree KV, typed tables+ACID+MVCC, stable file format; single active write transaction. redb4.3 added experimental-multiprocess; not a stable proven substitute for SQLite's direct process-sharing. Current Linux crate uses libc locks, so Rust engine does not imply freestanding stack/no C ABI. Default Immediate durability, optional weaker None/Eventual; quick-repair changes recovery/commit cost. https://github.com/cberner/redb and CHANGELOG.md.
Fjall3.1.12, Rust LSM KV, cross-keyspace atomicity, single-writer and optimistic serializable transaction APIs; one owning process (parallel file opening across processes prohibited). Default writes flush OS buffers, not stable disk; explicit SyncAll required for matched durable acknowledgement. LZ4 compression, optional key/value separation, background compaction. Online file/checkpoint backup issue52 remains open; logical snapshot copy is distinct. https://github.com/fjall-rs/fjall and https://github.com/fjall-rs/fjall/issues/52.
Turso Database (formerlyLimbo), actual Rust in-process SQLite-compatible engine, current README reports production users yet pre1.0. SQL/file/CAPI compatibility is partial; asyncio_uring, BEGIN CONCURRENT/MVCC, CDC, vector operations, experimental multiprocess .tshm. COMPAT documents STRICT,CHECK,TRIGGER,UPSERT,RAISE ABORT and our relevant PRAGMAs (synchronousOFF/FULL), manualBEGIN IMMEDIATE, but exactcompoundPK/trigger interactions unexecuted. sqlite3_backup API stubbed; VACUUM INTO supported. WITHOUT ROWID is limited but unused by Continuum so not evidence our schema fails. https://github.com/tursodatabase/turso, COMPAT.md, docs/manual.md. Distinguish older libSQL as SQLite fork, not fullyRust engine.
Heed wraps mature LMDB C; Rust RocksDB binding wraps C++ and native dependencies. DuckDB C++ embedded analytical SQL is a different primary workload. No new database benchmark, engine migration or generic backend framework has been authorized by this question's scope, although project R&D/doc publication is already authorized. Discussion should inform a reviewable research plan and preserve the ongoing real-use pilot. Do not invent unavailable GitHub/file access, source facts or received cross-chat consensus.
